construction.definition: In curvature -1 H^d initialize y_0=o=x_ref, I_0={o}, r_0=r, S_0=boundary B(o,r), and an orthonormal tangent basis e_i^(0). For k=1,...,d-1 set Delta_(k-1)=artanh(cos(theta)tanh(r_(k-1))), r_k=arsinh(sin(theta)sinh(r_(k-1))), y_k=exp_(y_(k-1))(Delta_(k-1)e_k^(k-1)), and transport every basis vector to y_k. Define I_k=gspan(y_0,...,y_k) and S_k={x in S_(k-1): angle(e_k^(k-1),log_(y_(k-1))(x))=theta}. Fix x* in S_(d-1). For k=0,...,d-2 let gtilde_k=-e_(k+1)^(k)/cos(theta), V_k=-gtilde_k-log_(y_k)(x*)/dist(y_k,x*), and L_k=exp_(y_k){v in T_(y_k)H^d: <V_k,v> >=0}. Set f(x)=dist(x,x*)+max_(i=0,...,d-2)dist(x,L_i)/cos(theta). This is Eq. (14), not the alternative C_k construction in Remark 31.
construction.hidden_objects: The minimizer x* and constructed halfspaces. The covered transcript stays in successively revealed I_k; no unrestricted information-theoretic claim is made.
model_membership_refs: Eq. (14), PDF p.24, explicitly declares global geodesic convexity and M-Lipschitzness.
Lemma 27, pp.22–23, and p.25 give x* in all L_i, so f*=f(x*)=0; x* in S_(d-1) subset boundary B(o,r).
construction.public_information: Ambient H^d, curvature -1, initialization o, r, epsilon, dimension d and M. Access to hidden halfspaces is not granted.

oracle_realizations.choices_and_history: Fix the function, including x*, before selecting responses along the deterministic history. A2 is required for that same Oracle trajectory; arbitrary Algorithms are not proved to satisfy it.
oracle_realizations.cost: T=d first-order queries, each returning a function value and subgradient. No Oracle implementation runtime guarantee.
oracle_realizations.information_bottleneck: A1 requires x_0=o and x_k in the gspan of previous queries and subgradients. A2 requires x_k in intersection_(ell<k)L_ell for k<=d-1. Inductively x_k in I_k and the selected g_k is tangent to I_(k+1), so the covered query span grows by at most one direction per response. This is a geometric support restriction, not a bound on arbitrary scalar information in function values.
oracle_realizations.information_to_error: Lemma 26 gives dist(x_k,x*)>=dist(y_k,x*)=r_k for x_k in I_k. Penalties vanish on the covered trajectory, hence f(x_k)-f*=dist(x_k,x*)>=r_k>=r/2=epsilon M r by Lemma 24.
oracle_realizations.query_and_feedback: Return exact f(x). At a covered query x_k in I_k and every L_i, k=0,...,d-2, set theta_(x_k)=angle(log_(x_k)(y_(k+1)),log_(x_k)(x*)), choose ghat_k=-sin(theta_(x_k))P_(y_k->x_k)V_k/(cos(theta)||V_k||), and return g_k=ghat_k-log_(x_k)(x*)/dist(x_k,x*). Lemma 28 makes this tangent to I_(k+1). All penalties vanish at the query, so the selected penalty term is active and g_k is an admissible subgradient of f. At x_k=y_k, ghat_k=-V_k and g_k=gtilde_k. The final budgeted query needs no further cancellation; elsewhere the Oracle may return any admissible subgradient. Locators: Lemma 28 pp.23–24 and induction p.25.
oracle_realizations.sampling_and_reuse: Exact responses for one fixed function; no sampling, stochastic noise or randomized lifting.
